need: Frontend UI detail, implementation, visual fidelity, and audit must preserve native destination semantics, approved progress presentation, and the hierarchy of compact numeric facts. A destination-bearing row needs a real non-null href and link semantics before render; progress declared by the approved contract cannot be flattened into a badge; compact scores and statuses remain subordinate to their owning section and content titles.
negativeBoundary: Do not make every card clickable, invent progress for categorical counts, force progressbars where no approved progress datum exists, fake a route from an opaque global id, or hard-code the Profile overview layout as a universal template.
acceptanceCriteria: A datum with an approved destination is frozen and rendered through the selected Grammar destination interface using native link semantics and a non-null real href; hover, focus, keyboard, and click proof expose the same destination.

Progress declared by the approved contract remains visibly represented by the approved progress semantic; a badge-only replacement fails detail and implementation unless upstream authority changes the datum.
Each content datum has a semantic rank, and compact numeric facts or statuses remain subordinate to their owning section and content titles instead of being concatenated into a stronger headline.
Visual fidelity and UI audit reject static destination rows, missing declared progress, or fact-over-title typography using DOM, accessibility, computed-style, and visible-browser evidence.

accepts: Course evidence is a native-link pressable surface whose canonical URL is available at hover time.
Approved course progress remains a visible progress presentation rather than a trailing count badge only.
Readiness percentage is a compact fact subordinate to the readiness section title and course label.
rejects: A static course div or button-only destination that cannot expose its URL before activation.
Removing approved progress because the row still displays completion numbers.
Joining a compact score with a content label into a headline that competes with its section title.

review.rationale: Visible Profile evidence proves three reusable regressions that passed prior review despite violating destination semantics, the approved course-progress contract, and fact-to-title hierarchy. Bind them before rerunning product visual fidelity.
